title: General Aptitude
summary: Common section in every GATE paper: 10 questions (5 x 1-mark + 5 x 2-mark) = 15 marks, MCQ/MSQ/NAT, 1/3 or 2/3 negative marking on wrong MCQs only. The GATE 2027 GA syllabus (IIT Madras) has four sections: Verbal Aptitude (grammar, vocabulary, reading comprehension, narrative sequencing), Quantitative Aptitude (data interpretation, numerical computation & estimation, mensuration & geometry, elementary statistics & probability), Analytical Aptitude (deduction/induction, analogy, numerical relations & reasoning) and Spatial Aptitude (translation, rotation, scaling, mirroring, assembling, grouping, paper folding/cutting, 2D/3D patterns). Questions are school-level but tricky; toppers score 12-15/15. Best ROI: ~40-60 hours spread over the prep period, mostly solving PYQs from all GATE branches (GA questions are identical in style across papers, so 100+ sets of PYQs exist).
notesGuide: Keep ONE slim GA notebook (or a single digital doc) with 4 tabs = the 4 syllabus sections. (1) Quant: a one-page formula sheet per topic (percent/ratio shortcuts, log & exponent rules, nPr/nCr + circular/identical-object cases, AP/GP sums, areas/volumes/surface areas, triangle & circle theorems, mean/median/mode/SD, basic probability rules) - write each formula with ONE worked PYQ beside it. (2) Verbal: a running 'error log' of grammar rules you got wrong (article/preposition/tense/subject-verb agreement) with the exact sentence, plus a vocabulary list of words/idioms from GATE PYQs (word, meaning, the PYQ sentence). (3) Analytical: a 'pattern bank' - for each PYQ type (syllogism/deduction, seating/arrangement, analogy, number relations) write the solving template in 3-5 steps and draw the diagram/table you used. (4) Spatial: sketch every paper-folding/cutting, cube-net, mirror/rotation PYQ by hand with the answer figure - redrawing builds the visual skill. Maintain a 'mistake log' table (date, source/PYQ id, topic, why wrong: concept/calculation/misread, fix) and revisit it weekly. Before each mock, re-read only the formula sheet + mistake log (15 min).

topics.title: Verbal: Grammar & Vocabulary
topics.tips: Usually 2-3 one-mark questions per paper - near-guaranteed marks. Read the whole sentence, identify the grammatical slot (tense/article/preposition) before reading options. Keep a PYQ vocabulary list; GATE reuses word families. Don't overthink: pick the most natural, formal English.

topics.title: Verbal: Reading Comprehension & Narrative Sequencing
subtopics: Main idea / which statement is supported
topics.tips: GATE RC passages are 4-8 lines; answers are 'what can be inferred' - choose the option that is strictly supported, never the one that is merely true in the real world. For sequencing, find the opening sentence (introduces a noun) and pronoun/connector links (however, this, thus) to chain sentences.

topics.title: Quant: Numerical Computation & Estimation
topics.tips: Largest share of GA marks. Memorise percent-fraction equivalents (1/8 = 12.5%, etc.), successive change formula a+b+ab/100, log rules, and nCr identities. Many are NAT - compute carefully and re-check units. For P&C, decide first: order matters? repetition allowed? identical objects? circular?

topics.title: Quant: Data Interpretation
topics.tips: Typically one 2-mark question. Read axis labels/units and the exact question (percentage of what?). Approximate first, then compute only if options are close. Practice with a timer: 3 minutes per DI question.

subtopics: Volumes & surface areas (cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, sphere)
topics.tips: Recent DA papers (2025, 2026) had shaded-area circle questions. Draw the figure, mark all known lengths/angles, decompose into standard shapes. Memorise sector area = (theta/360)*pi*r^2 and inscribed-angle theorem.

topics.title: Analytical Aptitude: Logic, Analogy & Numerical Reasoning
subtopics: Numerical relations & reasoning (puzzles, arrangements, ordering, ages)
topics.tips: Usually 2-3 questions, often 2-mark MSQ/MCQ puzzles. Always tabulate or draw (Venn diagram for syllogisms, grid for arrangements). For 'which must be true' check every option against the constraints; for MSQ there is no partial credit, so verify each option independently.

topics.title: Spatial Aptitude: Transformations, Folding & Patterns
topics.tips: Added to the syllabus from GATE 2024 and now appears every year (often 1-2 questions). Practice by physically folding/cutting paper and sketching. For cube nets: opposite faces are never adjacent in the net (skip one). For rotation, track one distinctive corner/marker instead of the whole figure.
